title: Vikky v. State of U.P.
coram: V.K. Shukla, J.; Shashi Kant, J.
docket: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 16672 of 2014
disposition: Quash of s.138(d) FIR refused; compounding left to Code and s.152.
headnote: The Allahabad High Court refused to quash an FIR under Section 138(d) of the Electricity Act, 2003 that disclosed a cognizable offence. Any arrest for an offence not entailing more than seven years must comply with Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A CrPC. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and Section 152 of the Act.
facts: Vikky approached the Allahabad High Court to quash an FIR dated 25 August 2014, Case Crime No. 585 of 2014, registered under Section 138(d) of the Electricity Act, 2003 at Police Station Kosikalan, District Mathura. He had not been arrested. His counsel argued that the alleged offence could not attract a sentence of more than seven years, so arrest should not be mechanical, and that the offence was compoundable. The State appeared through the Additional Government Advocate.

holding_units.topic: quashing FIR for interference with meters or works
holding_units.holding: An FIR registered under Section 138(d) of the Electricity Act, 2003 that discloses a cognizable offence will not be quashed. If arrest is to be effectuated for an offence that will not entail a sentence of more than seven years, the police must comply with Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A CrPC.
If the alleged offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and Section 152 of the Electricity Act, 2003.

not_decided.point: whether the alleged Section 138(d) offence is compoundable on the facts
not_decided.note: The Court left compounding to the petitioner if the offence is compoundable, without deciding that it is.
